hook_text: In 1976, schoolchildren picked up placards instead of pens, and a single photograph showed the world what apartheid really was.
clip_script: Soweto, Wednesday 16 June 1976. Thousands of students in school uniform march through the streets, singing. Their placards say "Down with Afrikaans". The government has ordered that half their subjects must be taught in Afrikaans, a language many of their teachers can't even speak. But it's about more than language. It's about overcrowded classrooms, too few books and a system called Bantu Education, designed to keep them down. Near Orlando West High School, the police block the road. Stones fly. Then the police open fire on the children. Twelve-year-old Hector Pieterson is shot. An older student, Mbuyisa Makhubo, carries him, his sister running beside them. A photographer takes one picture, and the whole world sees it. Today, 16 June is Youth Day.
visual_style: Students in school uniforms marching with handmade placards; a crowded 1970s classroom; police vans in a dusty street; the famous photograph recreated as a respectful illustration; the Hector Pieterson Memorial; young people today on Youth Day.
pacing: Upbeat marching rhythm at the start, sudden stop at the shooting, slow and reflective at the end.
